one_liner: Attio is a CRM for managing contacts, relationships, and workflows.

auth.notes: OAuth is preferred for apps serving multiple workspaces; workspace API keys and HTTP Basic authentication are also supported.

access.notes: API keys are available on all plans, including Free, but require workspace-admin permissions to create. An unpublished app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces; publication requires Attio review.

api.notes: The public JSON-over-HTTPS API supports reading and writing workspace information, with realtime events available through webhooks.

mcp.notes: Attio hosts an MCP server for access to Attio workspaces.

verdict.rationale: The Free plan and all-plan API-key availability establish a path to credentials, while Attio documents a public REST API for reading and writing workspace information. Public app publication requires review, but an unpublished app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces.

evidence.quote: Attio is a customizable CRM and workspace for managing your team's relationships and workflows.

You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces. If you are building an app for a single workspace, you can manually generate an API key to make requests on behalf of that workspace only.
We also support HTTP Basic Authentication, where the username is the token and the password is left blank.
Available on all plans. Admins can create and manage API keys.
The Free plan costs nothing for up to three users.
An unpublished app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces.
Publishing requires a review from the Attio team, which can take up to 1 week.
Attio provides a public REST API which exchanges JSON over HTTPS.
This allows developers to build apps that read and write information to and from Attio workspaces. You can also subscribe to events in realtime using webhooks.
Attio MCP is Attio’s hosted MCP server that gives AI tools secure access to your Attio workspace.

The quotes identify a public REST API and support the claimed reading, writing, and webhook capabilities.

Free-plan API keys and a documented public REST API support building now with no credential or API blocker. Publication review limits distribution, but unpublished apps can be installed without that review.
